text: gi: the near shadow box was fitted to the CENTROID OF A FRUSTUM SLICE - a point in mid-air on the camera's centre ray, 362 m above ground at cam=far. Boxes are square to the light, so that slid the covered ground 821 m along the sun's azimuth. Pads inside cascade 0: 1 of 8 -> 8 of 8, texel 0.801 -> 0.313 m, and the shipped config is CHEAPER: 197 draws / 1.171 M tris against 200 / 1.278 M.

Nobody had measured that trains.js raises engine.shadowNeedsUpdate 251 times a SECOND, so three's near shadow map redraws every frame. That single fact is what made the cascade fix look expensive. Filed to trains.js.

SEVENTH INERT RULE, and it was the charge itself: aWork cut/fill reads min=p50=max=0.000 on flat pads while 34% of the platform stands on fill; aux.z is a constant 1.000 over its own domain; wheel ruts were stroked at 0.56 px on a 1.12 m/texel map, below Nyquist; puddles were gated on a Laplacian that is 0 by construction on graded ground. Four dead mechanisms in one complaint.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN GUIDANCE: node --check does NOT catch the backtick trap. Six re-balanced backticks passed --check and the browser still refused the module. The gate that works is node -e import(file://...). I had given the wrong instruction to about a dozen rounds.

Vegetation: exposure was correctly signed all along - it is a SPIT DETECTOR. Sea fraction in a disc peaks on thin low tongues, so its 'most exposed' quartile is the island's LOWEST ground (mean altitude 0.371 vs 0.546 at Q3). It could not see a crest. Krummholz now real: density 398.9 -> 162.6 stems/ha, height 14.00 -> 8.82 m.

gi.js now ships setExposureLocked(). The adaptive exposure absorbs over half of any change and had invalidated numbers in three separate rounds - including the tank fill ratio filed as 78%-vs-44%, which measures 0.328 vs 0.332 with the stop frozen. Every colour measurement taken before today went through a moving meter.

The plant DOES cast shadows: +37.5 L on 2168 occluded pad pixels, 6.5% miss rate. Three probes said 0.00 L and all three were broken - castShadow and cascade layer bits are re-established by _adopt/_enrol on a 1 s clock, so the ablations were undone before the next frame.

PATTERN INSTANCE 6: rail's junctionBlock used a literal 32 m where a 1:6 lead is 4.49 m clear - inside the 5.00 m fouling threshold - while leadClearRun computed the correct value THIRTY LINES ABOVE IT. Cost: 40 uncoupled fouling pairs and passing loops that could not be used.

The 875 m parallel stretch never existed: tv-throat recorded the FIRST sample inside 5 m and the LAST and printed the difference. Actual contiguous runs: 37+38 m at the junctions, which is what a turnout is.

Loops verified working: soak 500 parses x 6 layouts PASS with all eight counters 0 and the crossovers FORCED ON - 34 workings on branch0/x1+x2, +16.6% distance. Uncoupled fouling pairs 40 -> 0 across all six layouts.

Blind 32: tank value trade judged RIGHT - 'the plant is currently the most legible thing on the island'. Form shading landed; the cast shadow is the remaining half. Dashboard verdict YES for the third round running.

BOTTLENECK IDENTIFIED, and the critic's explanation for it was wrong. Terrain normals are real (p50 tilt 6.4 deg, max 81.4) and 108 of 140 ground cells change >5 L when the sun moves dawn->dusk. The ground IS lit. It cannot show a terminator because half the island is within 6.4 deg of flat. Symptom real, cause misdiagnosed - refuted before a round was spent on it.
FIRST RESOLVED VERDICT IN 29 COMPARISONS: the surf. 'No longer the brightest element. The white tanks and horizon sky both read brighter. Verdict discharged.'

The island was a LID BY CONSTRUCTION: the channel carve rode inside the droplet-erosion array, which tapers to zero at the waterline, so every channel died over the last 10 m of elevation - exactly at the beach. Now its own term: 31 of 360 bearings carry flow to the water, beach notched 2.70 m at mouths vs 0.43 m elsewhere.

Drainage thresholds were ABOVE the top of their own distribution: log(acc) maxes at 5.25, FLOW_HI was 8.0, so kind=='stream' was unreachable and CARVE_DEPTH carved nothing. pctWatercourse 0.00 -> 1.17%, pctGully 0.26 -> 8.22%.

The wet band's cold grey was one line: sand = sandRaw * (1 - wetSand*0.95) stripped the warm strand tint exactly where the band is, so 'wet sand' was darkening grey shingle. R-B -11 -> +20, saturation 0.14 -> 0.22, dry strand bit-identical.

A rail round made NO EDIT and was right to: it measured the change requested, found the premise false, and produced a six-variant trade table showing the change ALONE would make the defect 1.5-2.4x worse. It located the real bug in a file it does not own - one line, worth 3x.

Terrain: the lee-shading term was aimed at the NOON axis while judged frames are at 09:00 with the sun in the NE - it was darkening the faces the key light was hitting. Measured on the old axis the spread was 0.28 L, below the 1.6 L noise floor: the term did nothing. Now driven by the live sun uniform.

The surf was a constant-width ribbon because the SEABED was a function of distance-from-shore alone - every stretch of coast had one profile, so 'depth-driven' was 'offset-driven'. Shelf width at 4.2 m depth now 133.7 +/- 33.3 (range 36-166), was 92.8 +/- 3.6.

Wet band at the judged pixel: -3.62 -> -27.99 L. And tq-value's wetBandDrop is now UNTRUSTWORTHY on this change - its window is 0-3 m but the band is 0-2.5 m, so its numerator contains bright dry sand. Ninth instrument failure, self-caught.

Sky: at FOG_P 1.5 the whole map sat in the toe of the curve - nothing was ever more than 15% hazed. FOG_H 130->400, FOG_P 1.5->3.0. B-R at 600-900 m now +9.3 against the reference's +11, verified independently.
CORRECTION (mine): the haze was NOT eating the waterline. A waterline pixel is 3.8% haze, not 92% - I misread an albedo-share figure as an atmosphere share and briefed a whole round on it.

CORRECTION (mine): the wing walls were never floating. A plan-grid daylight probe measured 0.6 m2 of hanging masonry before and after; what I read as daylight was the shadowed backs of the steps. The defect was real but my diagnosis was not.

Vegetation: the density rules were arithmetically INERT. The stand gate returned 1.000 at 100% of samples because its driving noise never leaves [0.40,0.72]; treeline 1.000 at 100%; slope gate >0.95 on 96.7%. The critic's 'exactly one density everywhere' was literally true in the code. Now three bands - open 143.6, margin 226.6, closed 380.7 stems/ha - with total population unchanged (7,017 vs 7,048). The forest was moved, not thinned.

Rock normals: winding inverted in Mesher.tube and _rockGeo. 15 of 52 solid meshes affected INCLUDING all 15 tree trunks, hidden because matBark is DoubleSide. Fixed at the winding, not by widening DoubleSide.

Trees 'level with the rail' had a different cause: terrain re-grades AFTER vegetation plants, and terrain's own note claimed vegetation was exempt from terrain:regraded. 164 stems >1 m out, worst 7.75 m beside a bore. Now re-seats 3,954 instances: 0 stems >1 m, worst 0.02 m.

grep in this shell is a function wrapping ugrep that returns NOTHING with exit 1 on a binary-looking file. A raw NUL byte at trains.js:2267 made the whole file unsearchable, silently, all session - it hid 41 lighting matches and produced a false claim. NUL replaced with an escape; file is text again.

Terrain: the wet band existed but rendered BRIGHTER than dry sand (drop 1.02). Two causes, one of them the identical roughness mistake the puddle term made two rounds earlier, documented 40 lines above it. Now 0.83.

The green train was the yard shunt: _stepShunt reversed the trip in ONE frame instead of over a turn state, teleporting the head 88.2 m and swapping the consist end for end. It was also invisible to the interlocking. Deleted. backwardsFrames 9 -> 4.

Four rounds dispatched on disjoint files: terrain (flat-sand material + station clipping + cliffs), rail (dead-end stubs, tunnel portals, bridges), trains (stuck green consist, passing loops, headlights), vegetation (planting over tunnels, rock normals, elevation rules).

Blind comparison #25: lost. Critic picked the reference, 'not close'. Single biggest gap named: the bare sand is one flat value over ~40% of the frame and never darkens - no slope shading, no wet band, no damp under canopy. Everything else is downstream of it.

rail.js bug fixed: earthworks() demoted short structures ignoring depth, so a short-but-deep tunnel became an illegal 23.3 m open cut against its own 9 m threshold. Deepest cut 23.3 -> 8.9 m, cuts over 9 m 2 -> 0.

FULL GATE PASS, verified independently: 498 parses x 6 layouts, collision/reversal/floating/unreachable/relayout/deadRailway/consoleErrors/edge all 0, 1,307,572 junction checks none skipped. That is the whole measurable half of gauntlet two.
Rail round landed: 45 earthwork spans declared (13 cut, 14 fill, 3 viaduct, 2 tunnel, 4014 m). Deepest cut 11.9 m, one span over the 9 m tunnel threshold. Dead-end rails gone - 0 dead tracks.
